html:
A movement of 1856 to 1857 in which the Xhosa people of the eastern Cape killed their cattle and burned their grain, following a prophecy, and suffered a terrible famine.

A teenage girl, Nongqawuse, said the ancestors had told her that if the people destroyed their cattle and crops, the dead would rise, new herds would appear, and the British would be swept into the sea. The Xhosa had lost land in a series of frontier wars, and a cattle disease was already killing their herds. The paramount chief Sarhili backed the prophecy.

Hundreds of thousands of cattle were killed. When the promised day passed, tens of thousands of people starved, and many more went into the Cape Colony to look for work. The governor, Sir George Grey, used the disaster to take Xhosa land for white settlers. It is often compared with other movements of hope under colonial pressure, such as the Ghost Dance in North America.
sum: A movement of 1856 to 1857 in which the Xhosa people of the eastern Cape killed their cattle and burned their grain, following a prophecy, and suffered a terrible famine.
